---
title: Playo
description: Playo External Venue Integration v2.0 — live. camelCase fields, a requestStatus envelope, and venue-local times.
---

**Status: live.** gamexo implements Playo's *External Venue Integration API
Specifications v2.0*. Seven endpoints, exercised end to end by an automated
consistency suite.

Their spec lists the endpoints the *venue* must host, so everything below is what
gamexo answers when Playo calls.

## Three things that differ from the rest of this API

Playo's contract is theirs, not ours, and three of its choices are load-bearing.

### camelCase everywhere

`courtId`, `startTime`, `paidAtPlayo`, `externalBookingId`. Not snake_case, which is
what every other part of gamexo uses.

### The `requestStatus` envelope

Every response carries a status field instead of relying on the HTTP status code:

```json
{ "requestStatus": 1, "message": "Orders confirmed.", "bookingIds": [] }
```

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `1` | Success |
| `0` | Failed — read `message` |

<Callout type="warn" title="A taken slot is a 200, not a 409">
  A slot that has just been sold answers `200 OK` with `requestStatus: 0`. This is
  deliberate and it is Playo's design: their client treats any non-2xx as a transport
  fault and retries it, and a court somebody else has bought never becomes available
  by retrying.

  Genuine faults — a bad API key, a malformed body, a crash — stay real HTTP errors.
  **Check `requestStatus` on every 200.**
</Callout>

<Callout type="info" title="One ambiguity in the spec">
  v2.0 documents `requestStatus` as `0 - failed, 1 - successful` in prose, while the
  sample payloads type it as `"string"`. gamexo sends **integers**, which is what the
  prose specifies and what the field means. Worth confirming before go-live.
</Callout>

### Local wall-clock time, split from the date

`"2026-09-04"` plus `"18:00:00"`, with no offset anywhere. That means the **venue's**
local time. Every conversion goes through the venue's own timezone, never the
server's.

## Authentication

```bash
X-API-Key: gx_playo_a1b2c3d4.iJ8pQr…
```

The key must have been issued for the `playo` dialect. A key issued for a different
contract is refused even if it is otherwise valid.

Requests carrying a `venueId` for a venue the key was not issued against are refused.

## Endpoints

All paths are relative to the base URL you were given, under `/api/v1/gateway`.

### Fetch availability

```http
GET /availability?date=2026-09-04&venue_id=…&sport_id=…
```

`date` is `YYYY-MM-DD` in venue-local time. `venue_id` and `sport_id` are optional
filters.

Reflects every booking at the venue — counter, dashboard, other platforms, and Playo
orders still in checkout. Expired holds are released before the read.

```json
{
  "requestStatus": 1,
  "message": "OK",
  "courts": [
    {
      "courtId": "5f2c…",
      "courtName": "Court 1",
      "slots": [
        {
          "startTime": "18:00:00",
          "endTime": "19:00:00",
          "price": "1200.00",
          "ticketsAvailable": 1
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Create an order (hold)

```http
POST /order/create
```

Blocks the courts while the customer pays on Playo. **Not** a booking: no revenue, no
counter entry, nobody expected to arrive.

```json
{
  "venueId": "…",
  "userName": "Ana Rao",
  "userMobile": "+919000011111",
  "userEmail": "ana@example.com",
  "orders": [
    {
      "courtId": "5f2c…",
      "date": "2026-09-04",
      "startTime": "18:00:00",
      "endTime": "19:00:00",
      "price": "1200.00",
      "paidAtPlayo": "1200.00",
      "playoOrderId": "PLY-88213"
    }
  ]
}
```

`endTime` is optional — their spec marks it so, and every court here is sold by the
hour, so it defaults accordingly.

Responds with `orderIds`, pairing your id with ours:

```json
{
  "requestStatus": 1,
  "message": "Orders created.",
  "orderIds": [{ "externalOrderId": "GX-4471", "playoOrderId": "PLY-88213" }]
}
```

All or nothing: if any slot fails, none are created and `requestStatus` is `0`.
Idempotent on `playoOrderId`.

<Callout type="warn">
  Holds expire after **15 minutes** if `/order/confirm` never arrives.
</Callout>

### Confirm an order

```http
POST /order/confirm
```

Turns held slots into real bookings once payment has cleared. Only after this do they
appear in reports, on the counter board and in the takings.

```json
{ "orderIds": ["PLY-88213"] }
```

Returns `bookingIds` pairing `externalBookingId` with `playoOrderId`.

All or nothing, and idempotent — confirming twice is a success, so a dropped response
is safe to retry. A lapsed hold still confirms if the court is free; it is refused
only once somebody else has taken the slot.

### Create a booking directly

```http
POST /booking/create
```

The single-phase flow, for venues integrated without the order/confirm handshake. A
confirmed booking straight away. Body is the same shape as `/order/create` with the
slots under `bookings`.

Same guarantees: all-or-nothing, idempotent on `playoOrderId`, same overlap
constraint.

### Cancel an order

```http
POST /order/cancel
```

```json
{ "orderIds": ["PLY-88213"] }
```

Releases held slots — and confirmed bookings too, because the spec requires this
endpoint to cancel a confirmed booking if one exists, so no order is left open on
Playo's side with no counterpart here. Idempotent.

### Cancel a booking

```http
POST /booking/cancel
```

```json
{
  "bookingIds": [
    {
      "externalBookingId": "GX-4471",
      "playoOrderId": "PLY-88213",
      "price": "1200.00",
      "refundAtPlayo": "1200.00"
    }
  ]
}
```

Frees the courts immediately. All or nothing, per the spec: *either all bookings
should be cancelled or none of the requested bookings*.

`price` and `refundAtPlayo` are recorded on the booking's timeline, not acted on — the
refund has already been made on Playo's side.

### Map booking ids

```http
POST /booking/map
```

Optional in the spec. Records Playo's own `playoBookingId`, which is a different value
from the `playoOrderId` already held, so reconciliation can match on whichever id
either side happens to be quoting.

## A typical flow

<Steps>
<Step>
**Read availability.** `GET /availability?date=2026-09-04` → `requestStatus: 1` with
courts and their free slots.
</Step>
<Step>
**Hold the slots.** `POST /order/create` with your `playoOrderId`. The courts are
blocked for 15 minutes and cannot be sold at the counter underneath you.
</Step>
<Step>
**Customer pays on Playo.** Nothing is expected from us during this.
</Step>
<Step>
**Confirm.** `POST /order/confirm` with the same `playoOrderId`. The hold becomes a
real booking and appears on the counter board and in the venue's takings.
</Step>
</Steps>

If the customer abandons checkout, send `/order/cancel` — or send nothing and let the
hold lapse after 15 minutes. Cancelling explicitly is better: it puts the court back
on sale immediately.

## Before go-live

- Confirm the `requestStatus` type question above.
- Confirm which flow you are using: order/confirm two-phase, or `/booking/create`
  single-phase.
- Make sure `playoOrderId` is stable across your own retries. It is the idempotency
  key, and an id that changes on retry defeats it entirely.
